features.title: Make your first video
features.lead: Start with the Master Node. Add other tools when you need them.
features.body:
• Load the starter workflow and select your model files.
  • Add a shot in the Master timeline; enter a prompt and duration.
  • Queue the workflow, review the take, then save with stock Create Video → Save Video.
features.detail: Models, uploaded media, optional providers and output files live on your ComfyUI server. This guide runs offline and does not generate video. Covers version 1.0.5; remote GPU generation was not verified.

features.title: Connect standard ComfyUI loaders
features.lead: Drop the downloaded JSON into ComfyUI.
features.body:
• Two Load Diffusion Model nodes feed fl2va_model and ref2va_model.
  • Load CLIP uses type minimax. Two Load VAE nodes supply video and audio.
  • Director Settings feeds config. Master images, audio and fps feed Create Video → Save Video.
features.detail: Install the package under ComfyUI/custom_nodes, install requirements using ComfyUI’s Python, and restart. ComfyUI must include native H3 generation, AddGuide, SigmaShift and current VIDEO APIs.

features.title: Choose the model family
features.lead: Use weights compatible with native MiniMax H3.
features.body:
• FL2VA: text-only, opening/closing images and Image Inpaint.
  • REF2VA: image/video/audio references and V2V/RV2V source edits.
  • Select the Qwen MiniMax text encoder, video VAE and audio VAE; choose matching files if your model paths differ.
features.detail: Use standard ComfyUI loaders. The Master records their checkpoint provenance internally for saved-shot reuse.

features.title: Generate your first shot
features.lead: Use one independent text-only shot before adding enhancements.
features.body:
• Set T2VA; enter a concrete action, scene and camera description.
  • Choose a short duration, a canvas divisible by 32, and a fixed seed. Use independent / clip-by-clip generation.
  • Queue, inspect the preview and status, then change one setting and rerun. Approve a take you want to keep.
features.detail: A take is one generated version of a shot. A latent is the compressed representation used during sampling; IMAGE frames are decoded pictures. Save the video through Video Combine.

features.title: Which mode should I use?
features.lead: Choose by the inputs you have.
features.body:
• T2VA: text. I2VA: opening image. FL2VA: opening + closing images. L2VA: closing image only.
  • REF2VA: image, video or audio references. V2V/RV2V: edit a source-video range.
  • Image Inpaint: generates one still using an image and a native five-frame pass.
features.detail: Endpoint images constrain the start/end. Reference media guides content without being an exact frame-by-frame copy. Image Inpaint has no general brush-mask workflow here.

features.title: Duration & resolution
features.lead: Generation uses 24 fps and a fixed frame grid.
features.body:
• Valid generated lengths: 5, 22, 39, 56, 73, 90, 107, 124… frames. Requests round upward.
  • Width and height must be divisible by 32. Manual chooses dimensions; Auto uses aspect + megapixels; Original snaps source dimensions to the grid.
  • Source edits are trimmed back to their actual source range. Playback FPS is an export setting.
features.detail: Auto aspect needs a reference/source size. Active working-resolution fields override basic settings.

features.title: Edit shots in the timeline
features.lead: Select a shot to edit its inspector.
features.body:
• Add, reorder or delete shots; set each prompt, mode, duration and seed.
  • Shared prompts/references apply across shots; local entries customize one shot.
  • Use per-shot brightness, contrast, saturation and audio gain/fades for finishing.
features.detail: Shared and local references are combined in resolved order. Grading and audio adjustments apply to decoded media; they do not change the model’s prompt.

features.title: Generate, preview & approve
features.lead: These controls have different jobs.
features.body:
• Generation selection: choose shots to run. Preview selection: choose media to inspect.
  • Approve/validate a completed take to reuse it; changing its inputs can invalidate reuse.
  • Changing a chained shot can invalidate downstream shots. Independent shots do not inherit that dependency.
features.detail: Validation marks a take as accepted; it does not score quality. Reuse requires matching inputs, model provenance and available cache files.

features.title: Keep or vary the seed
features.lead: A fixed seed makes comparisons easier.
features.body:
• Keep the same seed while comparing one setting.
  • Change the seed to request another variation; the editor preserves full 64-bit values.
  • Saved completed takes record their actual and next seeds for recovery.
features.detail: The same seed does not guarantee identical results across different models, settings, hardware or sampling paths.

features.title: Add & prepare reference media
features.lead: Upload, drag/drop or paste into the reference pool, then select for a shot.
features.body:
• Trim video/audio by start/end seconds; choose video, audio or both. The waveform shows decoded audio peaks.
  • Crop images/video using the rectangle or numeric fields. Scale with Off / Auto / Target / Fit / Fill; crop or pad to the required grid.
  • Set role and description. Subject/place/style/keyframe/pose are descriptive labels; pose is not a skeleton ControlNet.
features.detail: Limits: 9 images, 3 videos, 3 audios, 12 combined; each reference video and their total duration must be ≤15 seconds. Native H3 may impose additional combination constraints. Crops retain the original asset; picking a source frame uses the original player time.

features.title: Use RefMods & bundles
features.lead: Load an existing bundle; select its members as references.
features.body:
• Use <RefMod 1> or <RefMod 1:memberName> to mention a bundle/member.
  • Expanded members count toward the normal reference limits.
  • RefMods organize reference assets; this node does not train or create a new RefMod model.

features.title: Apply a LoRA to one shot
features.lead: Select compatible LoRA files and set model strength.
features.body:
• Attach up to 8 LoRAs per shot.
  • Start with a moderate strength; compare with the same seed.
  • LoRAs modify the model; reference assets and RefMods supply media.
features.detail: The strength control supports −10 to 10, but extremes are not recommended presets. This is model-only LoRA application, with no separate CLIP strength. File hashes participate in cache identity.

features.title: Write & link your prompt
features.lead: Describe what happens, then camera, environment and sound.
features.body:
• Example: A cyclist turns onto a wet street. Low tracking camera. Evening shop lights. Tires hiss on pavement.
  • Use raw text or structured editing; shared text supplies recurring instructions.
  • Mention selected media with the editor’s reference tokens. Check resolved_prompt to see what H3 receives.
features.detail: Reference numbering follows the resolved selected order, not arbitrary upload labels. Source-edit modes reserve Video 1 for the source; other videos shift accordingly. RefMod aliases expand into native reference mentions.

features.title: Draft prompts with Prompt Forge
features.lead: Generate a draft, review it, then apply it.
features.body:
• Choose a provider: local Transformers/GGUF, Ollama or a compatible API. Select images if the provider supports vision.
  • Edit draft cards for prompt, duration and mode before applying; stale drafts are rejected when their source context changed.
  • For graph use: Local Prompt Model → Prompt Forge Draft → Review / Apply Prompt Draft; explicitly enable apply and choose append/replace.
features.detail: Provider requests run on the server: localhost means the remote ComfyUI machine. Local models do not auto-download. UI keys remain in the panel, but graph key widgets can be serialized in workflows. Avoid wiring a draft back into the same Master through a graph cycle; use a snapshot or the editor draft flow.

features.title: Edit part of an existing video
features.lead: Load a source, divide it into ranges, then select ranges to regenerate.
features.body:
• Use V2V/RV2V and describe the desired edit. The source becomes reference Video 1.
  • Split at the playhead, split equally or use optional scene detection. Merge only contiguous ranges from the same file.
  • Leave other ranges unselected for source passthrough; generated ranges are trimmed to the source length.
features.detail: There is no generic source-latent strength slider. Automatic continuity prefixes are disabled for source edits. Scene detection needs scenedetect[opencv]. To extend a video, use locked source Clip 0, then add generated shots. Source ranges keep original-time coordinates.

features.title: Connect consecutive shots
features.lead: Choose independent shots or continuity from the previous take.
features.body:
• Independent shots begin separately; chained shots use a saved tail as their prefix.
  • Context choices 5 / 22 / 39 / 56 are pixel frames. The generated prefix is trimmed from the delivered shot.
  • Use a compatible completed take; inspect transitions before approving the sequence.
features.detail: The tail supplies context, not an exact motion guarantee. Prefix trim and previous trim are saved for later project assembly.

features.title: Place a guide at a time
features.lead: Use Shot Extras to choose a guide reference and timestamp.
features.body:
• Enter the guide time in seconds inside the visible shot.
  • The native AddGuide path offsets the anchor for a continuity prefix.
  • Check the reference and timestamp when an anchor lands at the wrong point.
features.detail: This is a timestamped native guide, not an additional guide-strength control.

features.title: Save, resume & branch takes
features.lead: Completed takes are cached automatically.
features.body:
• Load Take Checkpoint: choose project ID, clip ID and latest or an explicit take UUID.
  • Connect a checkpoint to continue from that take. Use explicit IDs for a branch.
  • Advance Staged Take returns staged when its gate is true; otherwise it returns current.
features.detail: Cache contains completed media/latents and manifests. It cannot resume an unfinished sampler step. Missing files or changed inputs prevent reuse. Advance does not judge which take looks better.

features.title: Choose what to export
features.lead: Workflow wiring, project authoring and generated takes are separate.
features.body:
• Workflow JSON: graph and node settings. Lightweight project JSON: timeline/settings with asset and cache hints.
  • Portable .mmxproj: includes reference/source bytes; excludes models and heavy generated takes.
  • Append remaps incoming IDs; overwrite replaces authoring. New Project / Reset Timeline / Clear Cache have different scopes.
features.detail: Clear Cache removes generated takes while retaining uploaded assets. Appended shared references become local to imported shots. Back up generated-take storage separately when moving servers.

features.title: Where to connect enhancements
features.lead: Configuration packs go into Master; pixel tools receive IMAGE frames.
features.body:
• During sampling: optional model Cache, then SelfLift.
  • After sampling: latent Refine, decode/grading, then FaceRefine.
  • After Master: Pixel / RTX, Playback / Watermark / Loop, then Video Combine.
features.detail: Add one stage at a time and compare with a fixed seed. Acceleration Cache is separate from saved project takes.

features.title: SelfLift: switch to higher resolution
features.lead: Connect SelfLift to the Master’s selflift input.
features.body:
• Start at lowres_scale 0.5; reserve 4 high-resolution steps as an initial trial.
  • Choose the split with highres_steps or transition_step. Use a compatible model_hires override only when needed.
  • Use interpolation or compatible learned latent weights; tiling/chunking can reduce working memory.
features.detail:
The weight dropdown has no explicit “interpolate” entry: when no weights are installed, its unset placeholder falls back to interpolation. native_low_carry reuses compatible low-resolution context only for chained shots. rho=0 disables the optional pixel-anchor mix; w_min/w_max bound its weighting.

ControlMeaning
lowres_scaleSpatial scale of the initial stage.
highres_steps / transition_stepChoose the resolution-switch location.
native_low_carryReuse low-resolution context between compatible chained shots.
rhoEnable/control mixing with a VAE pixel-anchor path.
w_min / w_maxBounds for the anchor mix weighting.
model_hiresOptional MODEL for the high-resolution stage.
tiling / chunkingSpatial sampling tiles and learned-latent temporal chunks.

features.title: Refine an existing latent
features.lead: Connect Refine to the Master’s refine input.
features.body:
• refine: another sampling pass. upscale: enlarge then refine. latent_upscale: enlarge without diffusion.
  • Start with one pass; adjust target size, steps and denoise. Default controls include 3 steps and denoise 0.45.
  • Global backend plans tiles from the memory budget; sampler backend uses explicit tile_count/overlap.
features.detail:
Optional refine_model must be compatible. SIGMAS must be 1D, finite, nonnegative and nonincreasing, with ≥2 entries. More passes (1–20) cost compute and can drift.

ControlUse
refine_modelOptional compatible model for later refinement.
passesRepeat refinement; supported range is 1–20.
sampler / schedulerChoose the refine sampling procedure.
SIGMAS inputSupply an explicit noise schedule.
global backendMemory-aware planner and temporal/spatial refinement.
sampler backendExplicit native sampling alternative with per-step spatial tiles.
upscale_precisionauto, bf16, fp16 or fp32 for learned latent weights.

features.title: Learned upscaling, tiles & chunks
features.lead: Install compatible H3 latent weights under models/latent_upscale_models.
features.body:
• Weights must match the supported 24-channel 3D architecture; arbitrary image upscalers do not work here.
  • Spatial tiles overlap and blend. Temporal chunks reduce memory but may change attention/normalization behavior.
  • Choose auto / bf16 / fp16 / fp32 precision as supported; use interpolation when learned weights are unavailable.
features.detail: Supported checkpoint extensions: .safetensors, .sft, .pt, .pth. Loading validates architecture. Audio stays separate from visual latent enlargement.

features.title: Refine one tracked face
features.lead: Connect FaceRefine to the Master’s face_refine input.
features.body:
• Select a compatible face detector; choose largest-face or centre-most initial selection.
  • Set crop size/context, prompt and sampling strength; preview the tracked result.
  • Control pasted region, feather/dilation, color matching and blend. Blend 0 preserves the base frames.
features.detail:
Tracks one face, samples native audiovisual crops and keeps the main audio. No detections means a reported skip; a missing detector is a setup error. Inherit or offset the shot seed; stitching fades edits near boundaries.

ControlEffect
confidence / selectDetection threshold; initial largest-face or centre-most selection.
crop_factor / crop_sizeHow much surrounding context is sampled.
canvas_modeManual crop canvas or an automatically capped one.
paste_regionFace rectangle, ellipse or full crop.
mask_dilation / featherExpand and soften the pasted region.
colour_match / blendMatch crop color and control how much to paste.
steps / sampler / scheduler / SIGMASSampling of the face crop; separate from the main pass.

features.title: Semantic Bridge & acceleration Cache
features.lead: Both affect generation; neither is a prompt writer.
features.body:
• Semantic Bridge: install the exact student checkpoint under models/semantic_bridge; connect the pack and set alpha (default 0.15).
  • Cache: connect the model acceleration configuration; adjust reuse threshold, active interval, maximum cached steps and device.
  • Compare quality against a baseline: reused model computation can introduce artifacts.
features.detail: Semantic Bridge adapts conditioning tokens. Cache defaults include threshold 0.05, start 0.15, end 0.90 and max steps 2. Its model hook depends on installed ComfyUI compatibility; no measured speedup is promised.

features.title: Enlarge decoded frames
features.lead: Master images → Pixel / RTX → exporter images.
features.body:
• bicubic: resize. learned_pixel: supply an UPSCALE_MODEL.
  • RTX VSR / RTX High Bitrate: require their optional providers and compatible hardware/runtime.
  • Set target width/height; keep the Master audio connected separately to the exporter.
features.detail: Bicubic and learned-pixel paths resize to the target, including stretching. resize_method applies to RTX providers. These tools work on pixels, unlike SelfLift/latent Refine.

features.title: Use the correct Master output
features.lead: Normal video export uses images + audio.
features.body:
• images/audio: assembled selected sequence. fps/frame_count: delivered timing.
  • positive/latent/resolved_prompt: final shot only. status: execution report.
  • project_state: timeline JSON. video: VHS_VIDEOINFO metadata, not playable VIDEO.
features.detail: For a genuine VIDEO socket, connect images, audio and fps to stock Create Video. Final latent precedes decoded grading and FaceRefine; it is not a concatenation of all finished shots.

features.title: Save a playable video
features.lead: Connect images and audio to Video Combine & Audio Muxer.
features.body:
• Set FPS, filename prefix, container and codec; enable save_output for permanent output rather than temp.
  • Use MP4 + H.264 for a first compatibility test. Other options include MKV/WebM/animated WebP/AVIF, H.265/VP9/AV1 and 8/10-bit paths.
  • Choose audio codec, metadata, crop-to-audio or ping-pong as needed.
features.detail: PyAV is default; FFmpeg is an explicit fallback. Codec/container support depends on installed builds. Audio options include Auto/AAC/Opus/MP3/FLAC. Passthrough frames does not disable encoding; preview transcodes can differ from the saved codec.

features.title: Export an entire saved project
features.lead: Master project_state → Project / Shot Video Export.
features.body:
• Choose all or selected shots, export FPS and optional individual shot files.
  • Select final, pre_refine or original_source stream.
  • Export assembles saved shots one at a time; generate missing takes before exporting.
features.detail: Final is the finished cached take; pre_refine uses its saved first-pass stream; original_source uses source ranges. Missing pre-refine can fall back to source when present. Assembly normalizes the canvas and uses H.264 MP4 with FFmpeg concatenation; it needs the original cache/assets.

features.title: Change playback FPS
features.lead: Master frames/audio → Playback / Watermark / Loop → exporter.
features.body:
• resample: repeat/drop frames to preserve duration; this is not AI motion interpolation.
  • retime: change speed and audio pitch; the waveform is resampled.
  • Set exporter FPS to the processing output’s timing.

features.title: Watermark & loop
features.lead: Configure the same Output Processing node.
features.body:
• Choose text or a logo, corner and opacity; a supplied logo takes precedence.
  • For loops, overlap end and beginning and crossfade picture + audio.
  • Overlap 0 disables looping; positive overlap must be less than half the clip. Output becomes shorter by the overlap.
features.detail: Example: 124 frames with 12-frame overlap produces 112 frames. Check the seam and sound before saving.

features.title: Override a model per shot
features.lead: Use Shot Model Pack → Master model_pack.
features.body:
• Give each compatible model entry a name; select that name on the shot.
  • SelfLift model_hires and Refine refine_model affect their own stages.
  • Keep model family/encoder compatibility consistent with the shot mode.

features.title: Connect external shot prompts
features.lead: Use these when you need inputs outside the timeline editor.
features.body: Connect a standard STRING output to Master prompt_text. Use one prompt per line; blank lines are ignored. No adapter node is needed.
features.detail: Image-family groups precede reference-family groups when both are supplied directly. RefPack can hold graph multimedia inputs and local selections; the bridge adapts IMAGE inputs into reference entries.

features.title: Advanced conditioning & sampling
features.lead: Use only for a custom sampling graph.
features.body:
• Use the Master’s Conditioning Guide Output to produce conditioning for manual sampling.
  • Director Settings provides sampling controls. Tail From Latent extracts manual continuation tails.
  • Native MiniMax H3 conditioning nodes are available in ComfyUI for standalone manual graphs.
features.detail: Use Load Take Checkpoint for durable continuation. Custom guide dictionaries are advanced inputs, not a normal Master media output. Match socket types and avoid graph cycles.

features.title: Three useful workflows
features.lead: Try each with a short shot first.
features.body:
• Story: create 3 shots → approve shot 1 → chain 2 and 3 → export cached final shots.
  • Source edit: split a source → select one range → V2V/RV2V → leave other ranges as passthrough → assemble.
  • Upscale comparison: save a baseline → compare SelfLift, latent Refine and pixel enlargement separately with matching inputs.

features.title: Find the failing stage
features.lead: Read status first; isolate one optional stage at a time.
features.body:
• Model/input error: check family, encoder/VAE, reference limits and canvas/frame grid.
  • Missing take/export: regenerate the shot or restore its cache/assets. Provider error: check server-side models, URL and dependencies.
  • Out of memory: shorten the shot, lower resolution, use tiles/chunks, then retry before increasing quality settings.
features.detail: Face detection requires detector dependencies and weights; RTX needs its provider. If a movie has wrong timing, compare fps/frame_count, Output Processing policy and exporter FPS. Inspect exact socket types when a connection fails.

features.title: Before a long run
features.lead: Confirm these four things.
features.body:
• A short take generates and saves successfully with the selected model/encoders.
  • Reference mentions resolve correctly; approved takes and source assets remain available.
  • Transitions, sound and export FPS look right; there is enough server storage for completed takes.
features.detail: Save workflow and project authoring; back up media/take storage separately. Add optional stages only after the basic pipeline works.
